title: Clip a wafer onto an e-beam evaporator's sample plate and load it face down
instruction: Mount the wafer on the sample plate for e-beam evaporation, load it into the load lock once its light is green, then shut and lock the door. Tighten each clip screw 300 to 420 degrees; keep the door open under 2 minutes in all.
context: The evaporator coats from below, so the wafer hangs face down: it must be centred and held by clips that bite its round edge, enough of them, with screws that fit and are snug but not so tight they crack it. An open load lock takes on air and water that slow its pump-down and load the main chamber. Its light tower shows blue while a process runs (keep the door shut), green when it is done, orange for a warning and red for an error (tell the staff first).
setup: Bench top as the origin's level; angles on the plate are measured from +x (towards the load lock), 90 degrees towards the left arm. Loading stand (painted steel, fixed) at (0.18, 0) m, its top 130 mm high, with a socket that takes the plate's boss. On it, face up: a stainless sample plate 200 mm across and 1.5 mm thick (0.36 kg) with rings of tapped holes for other wafer sizes, and eight steel swing clips (13 x 4 x 1 mm tabs) in its 4 inch ring, 59.5 mm out, every 45 degrees, each on an M4 hex-head screw (7 mm across flats, 3 mm tall, a white paint mark on its top), parked along the rim with its screw loose. The 225 degree clip's screw is too long: its head stands 8 mm proud. On the plate: a 100 mm silicon wafer, pattern up, its primary flat facing the 90 degree clip, its centre 5 mm off the plate's centre towards 202.5 degrees. A 7 mm steel nut driver (hex socket 2.8 mm deep with a chamfered mouth, 12 mm across; round 5 mm shaft, 52 mm long overall; red round 12 mm handle 14 mm long; 35 g) stands socket down in a black block holder (30 x 30 x 60 mm, 12.2 mm square hole 10 mm deep, fixed) at (0.12, -0.17). Load lock (painted steel, fixed, glass viewport on top): a box 0.28 m deep (x = 0.36 to 0.64 m), 0.76 m wide and 350 mm tall. The load lock has just been vented. Its front opening, 0.75 m wide and 100 to 320 mm above the bench, is closed by an aluminium door (6 mm thick, 0.25 kg) that slides up 250 mm, with a 12 mm round handle bar 25 mm in front, 200 mm high when shut. It starts shut and locked by a black T-shaped twist lock on the door's front, right of the handle (its bar's centre at (0.336, -0.20), 150 mm up when shut): upright it holds the door on its seat; a quarter turn clockwise (seen from the robot) lays it level and frees the door. Lifted to the top, a latch holds the door open; pulled 25 mm down off the latch (about 8 N), it slides down under its own weight. On the load lock's top at (0.40, 0.30) stands a light tower (red, orange, green, blue, top to bottom); a lit lamp's bright lens stands out of its band. Blue is lit at the start, green from 8 s on. Inside, a steel holder on a centre shaft at (0.485, 0): two arcs 170 mm high between low fences. On it lies an aluminium ring holder (220 mm across, 180 mm inside, 4 mm thick, 0.14 kg) with a 1.5 mm recess under its rim that fits the plate.
scoring: Measured at the end, once the plate, wafer, ring holder and door have moved under 1 mm in the last 1 s; 0 if not. 0 if, at any time, the long screw was turned over 90 degrees, a swung-in clip's screw was turned over 420 degrees (the wafer cracks), the door was lifted (over 3 mm off its seat) while the light was blue or was open more than 120 s in all, the wafer left its seat on the plate (centre over 8 mm off, or lifted), the plate or ring holder fell below 100 mm, or a fingertip came within 4 mm of the wafer's pattern (inside its 5 mm edge exclusion); 0 if the nut driver is inside the load lock. Otherwise 0 unless the wafer is centred on the plate (within 2 mm) and held by clips that leave no gap over 150 degrees round it: a clip holds if it was swung in past 70 degrees, then its screw turned at least 300 degrees clockwise, and its tip lies at least 2 mm inside the wafer's outline. 0.25 for that; 0.5 if also the ring holder lies face down on the load lock's holder (within 5 degrees, centre within 4 mm) carrying the plate face down (centred on it within 3 mm); 0.75 if also the door is shut (within 3 mm of its seat) and locked (its lever turned back within 10 degrees); 1.0 if also every fingertip is 5 cm from the door's handle and its lock.
reset_notes: One fixed layout; nothing is consumed. Clips start parked open with loose screws; the load lock starts vented, its door shut and locked, its light blue.
fidelity: Screws turn on hinges (no threads) and do not move in or out: a clip is tight once its screw turns 300 degrees after it is swung in, which then holds the clip; past 420 the wafer cracks. A lip under each tab keeps the wafer from sliding out, in place of clamping. The door's top latch is a spring that lets go when pulled 25 mm down; the twist lock holds the door shut by a stiff spring. The wafer collides as strips 1 mm inside its outline. Venting, pumping and the transfer arm are left out.
